message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑known dominant traits is the presence of a mane in adult males. The mane is a secondary sexual characteristic that is expressed when the dominant allele for mane development is present. While many other traits (coat color, size, etc.) are influenced by multiple genes and environmental factors, the mane’s expression is a classic example of a dominant genetic trait in lions.
